plain_english_revision: **What the amendment does:** This bill creates a new set of criminal offenses specifically targeting adults with disabilities in Alabama. It defines three degrees of abuse/neglect and three degrees of financial exploitation, each with escalating penalties depending on severity (e.g., Class A felony for first-degree abuse causing serious injury). The amendment also sets a 7-year statute of limitations for prosecutions and clarifies jurisdiction across counties.
candidate_position_supported: **Policy effect:** Expands the scope of criminal liability to include intentional or reckless abuse/neglect and financial exploitation of adults with disabilities, with tiered penalties based on harm severity. Introduces a dedicated legal framework (Alabama Adults with Disabilities Protection Act) to address gaps in existing elder-abuse protections.
evidence_quotes: **Definition of abuse/neglect:** 'The failure of a caregiver to provide food, shelter, clothing, medical services, medication, or health care for an adult with a disability.'

**Financial exploitation threshold:** 'The financial exploitation ... in which the value of the property taken exceeds two thousand five hundred dollars ($2,500) constitutes [first-degree] exploitation.'
**Statute of limitations:** 'Any prosecution brought for financial exploitation ... shall be commenced within seven years after the commission of the offense.'
review_reason: All definitions, penalties, and procedural rules are explicitly stated in the amendment text.
